messages.task:
You are a financial analysis assistant.  You have access to several read-only tools that expose operating-expense information stored in a synthetic corporate ledger.  Use the tools to retrieve any numbers you might need, perform the appropriate intermediate calculations, and finally answer the question with a single concise value.

Scenario
A rail-transport company reports its operating expenses by category.  Narrative disclosures for recent years include the following (table data are not shown here):
• Operating expenses increased $348 million in 2012 versus 2011.  Depreciation, wage and benefit inflation, higher fuel prices, and volume-related trucking services contributed to higher expenses.  Efficiency gains and weather-related savings partially offset the increase.
• Operating expenses increased $1.8 billion in 2011 versus 2010.  Fuel price per gallon rose 36 % during 2011, accounting for $922 million of the increase.  Wage and benefit inflation, volume-related costs, depreciation, and property taxes also contributed.
• Compensation and benefits include wages, payroll taxes, health and welfare costs, pension costs, other post-retirement benefits, and incentive costs.  Expenses in 2012 were essentially flat versus 2011 as operational improvements offset inflation.
• Fuel expense reflects locomotive diesel prices (which averaged $3.22 per gallon in 2012 and $3.12 in 2011) and volume measured in gross ton-miles.
• Purchased services and materials consist of costs of services purchased from outside contractors and other service providers.

Tools available
(listed alphabetically)
• calculate_percentage(part: float, whole: float) → float
  Return what percentage "part" is of "whole".
• compute_difference(new_value: float, old_value: float) → float
  Simple arithmetic helper that yields new_value – old_value.
• get_all_quarterly_expenses(category: str, year: int) → dict[int, float]
  Retrieve all four quarterly amounts for a category & year.
• get_average_quarterly_expense(category: str, year: int) → float
  Average of the four quarterly amounts (may not be needed).
• get_quarterly_expense(category: str, year: int, quarter: int) → float
  Retrieve a single quarterly amount.
• get_yearly_expense(category: str, year: int) → float
  Convenience wrapper that sums the four quarters and returns the annual total.
• list_all_categories() → list[str]
  Names of every expense category in the ledger.
• list_categories_above_threshold(year: int, threshold: float) → list[str]
  Categories whose annual total exceeds a given threshold.
• list_years_for_category(category: str) → list[int]
  All fiscal years for which quarterly data exist for a given category.

Question
The company wonders: "The 2011-to-2012 change in equipment and other rents is what percent of the total expense increase in 2012?"

Using the tools, compute the requested percentage and respond with a single value formatted like "8.6%" (one decimal place followed by the percent sign).
